text:
The mass of iron converted into $Fe_{3}O_{4}$ by the action of 18 g of steam is:

(Given: Molar mass of H, O and Fe are 1, 16 and 56 g mol$^{−1}$ respectively)

Assume iron is present in excess:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The reaction of iron with steam is:

$3Fe+4H_{2}O\to Fe_{3}O_{4}+4H_{2}$

We are given:

$\text{Mass of steam}=18\text{g}$

Molar mass of water:

$H_{2}O=2(1)+16=18\text{g mol}^{-1}$

So, moles of steam are:

$\text{Moles of}H_{2}O=\frac{18}{18}=1\text{mol}$

From the balanced equation:

$4\text{mol}H_{2}O\text{react with}3\text{mol}Fe$

Therefore, for $1$ mol $H_{2}O$:

$\text{Moles of Fe required}=\frac{3}{4}$

Now, molar mass of iron is:

$56\text{g mol}^{-1}$

So, mass of iron reacted:

$\text{Mass of Fe}=\frac{3}{4}\times 56=42\text{g}$

Hence, the mass of iron converted into $Fe_{3}O_{4}$ is:

$42\text{g}$

So, the correct option is:

$\text{Option D}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
What is the energy (in J atom$^{−1})$ required for the following process?
 $Li^{2+} (g)$ → $Li^{3+} (g) + e^{−}$
 (Take the ionization energy for the H atom in the ground state as $2.18\times 10^{-18}\text{J atom}^{-1}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the process

$\text{Li}^{2+}(g)\to \text{Li}^{3+}(g)+e^{-}$

we have to remove the only electron present in $\text{Li}^{2+}$.

$\text{Li}^{2+}$ is a hydrogen-like species because it has only one electron.

For a hydrogen-like species, ionization energy is given by

$E=Z^{2}\times 2.18\times 10^{-18}\text{J atom}^{-1}$

where $Z$ is the atomic number.

For lithium, $Z=3$.

So,

$E=3^{2}\times 2.18\times 10^{-18}$

$E=9\times 2.18\times 10^{-18}$

$E=19.62\times 10^{-18}$

$E=1.962\times 10^{-17}\text{J atom}^{-1}$

Hence, the required energy is

$1.962\times 10^{-17}\text{J atom}^{-1}$

So, the correct option is:

$\text{Option C}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I): The correct sequence of bond lengths in the following species is :
$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}<\mathrm{O}{}_{2}<\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}<\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$
Statement (II): The correct sequence of number of unpaired electrons in the following species is :
$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Bond order $=\dfrac{1}{2}(N_{b}-N_{a})$, and bond length decreases as bond order increases. Beyond 14 electrons the order of filling is $σ_{1s},σ_{1s}^{\ast },σ_{2s},σ_{2s}^{\ast },σ_{2p_{z}},π_{2p_{x}}=π_{2p_{y}},π_{2p_{x}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}}^{\ast },σ_{2p_{z}}^{\ast }$, so $N_{b}=10$ for all four species.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (15 electrons): one electron in $π^{\ast }$, $N_{a}=5$, bond order 2.5, 1 unpaired electron.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ (16 electrons): $(π_{2p_{x}}^{\ast })^{1}(π_{2p_{y}}^{\ast })^{1}$, $N_{a}=6$, bond order 2, 2 unpaired electrons.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ (17 electrons): $(π_{2p_{x}}^{\ast })^{2}(π_{2p_{y}}^{\ast })^{1}$, $N_{a}=7$, bond order 1.5, 1 unpaired electron.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$ (18 electrons): $(π_{2p_{x}}^{\ast })^{2}(π_{2p_{y}}^{\ast })^{2}$, $N_{a}=8$, bond order 1, no unpaired electron.

Bond order falls in the order $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$, so bond length is $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}<\mathrm{O}{}_{2}<\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}<\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$: Statement I is true.

The unpaired electrons give $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}=\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}>\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$; Statement II places $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ above $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}$, so it is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Consider the following data.
(i) $2\text{Al(s)}+6\text{HCl(aq)}\to \text{Al}_{2}\text{Cl}_{6}\text{(aq)}+3\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}+1200\text{kJ/mol}$
(ii) $\text{H}_{2}\text{(g)}+\text{Cl}_{2}\text{(g)}\to 2\text{HCl(g)}+164\text{kJ/mol}$
(iii) $\text{HCl(g)}+\text{aq}\to \text{HCl(aq)}+83\text{kJ/mol}$
(iv) $\text{Al}_{2}\text{Cl}_{6}\text{(s)}+\text{aq}\to \text{Al}_{2}\text{Cl}_{6}\text{(aq)}+663\text{kJ/mol}$
The enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid $\text{Al}_{2}\text{Cl}_{6}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In each equation the heat term is written on the product side, which means that heat is evolved; so every enthalpy change is negative:

(i) $2~\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s})+6\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq})\longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{6}(\mathrm{aq})+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$; $\Delta H_{1}=-1200\text{kJ}$

(ii) $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$; $\Delta H_{2}=-164\text{kJ}$

(iii) $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{aq}\longrightarrow \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq})$; $\Delta H_{3}=-83\text{kJ}$

(iv) $\mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{6}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{aq}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{6}(\mathrm{aq})$; $\Delta H_{4}=-663\text{kJ}$

Here "aq" stands for a large excess of water, so (iii) and (iv) are enthalpies of solution.

The target $2~\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s})+3\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{6}(\mathrm{s})$ is (i) + 3 $\times$ (ii) + 6 $\times$ (iii) $-$ (iv): $3~\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$, $6~\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$, $6~\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq})$ and $\mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{6}(\mathrm{aq})$ cancel.

$\Delta _{f}H=-1200+3(-164)+6(-83)-(-663)$

$\Delta _{f}H=-1200-492-498+663=-1527\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
19.5 g of fluoro acetic acid (molar mass = 78 g mol$^{−1})$ is dissolved in 500 g of water at 298 K. The depression in the freezing point of water was $1^{$∘}C. What is $K_{a}$ of fluoro acetic acid?

 (For water, $K_{f}=1.86$ K kg mol$^{−1})$. Assume molarity and molality to have same values.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given:

Mass of fluoroacetic acid $=19.5\text{g}$

Molar mass $=78\qquad \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Mass of water $=500\text{g}=0.5\text{kg}$

Depression in freezing point, $\Delta T_{f}=1^{\circ }\text{C}=1\text{K}$

$K_{f}=1.86\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$

We have to find $K_{a}$ of fluoroacetic acid.

First, calculate the number of moles of acid:

$n=\frac{19.5}{78}=0.25\text{mol}$

Now, molality of the solution:

$m=\frac{0.25}{0.5}=0.5\text{mol kg}^{-1}$

For an electrolyte,

$\Delta T_{f}=iK_{f}m$

So,

$1=i\times 1.86\times 0.5$

$1=i\times 0.93$

$i=\frac{1}{0.93}\approx 1.075$

Fluoroacetic acid is a weak monoprotic acid:

$\text{HA}⇌\text{H}^{+}+\text{A}^{-}$

If degree of dissociation is $α$, then for this type of acid:

$i=1+α$

Therefore,

$α=i-1=1.075-1=0.075$

Now use Ostwald’s dilution law:

$K_{a}=\frac{Cα^{2}}{1-α}$

Given in the question, assume molarity and molality are same, so

$C=0.5$

Thus,

$K_{a}=\frac{0.5\times (0.075)^{2}}{1-0.075}$

$=\frac{0.5\times 0.005625}{0.925}$

$=\frac{0.0028125}{0.925}\approx 3.04\times 10^{-3}$

So,

$K_{a}\approx 3\times 10^{-3}$

Hence, the correct option is:

$3\times 10^{-3}$

Option D.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
The solubility product constants of $\mathrm{Ag}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}$ and $\mathrm{AgBr}$ are $32x$ and $4y$ respectively at 298 K.

The value of  $\left (\frac{\text{molarity of}\mathrm{Ag}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}}{\text{molarity of}\mathrm{AgBr}}\right )$ can be expressed as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the molar solubility of $\mathrm{Ag}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}$ be $s_{1}$.

For the dissolution:

$\mathrm{Ag}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}(\mathrm{s})⇌2\mathrm{Ag}^{+}+\mathrm{CrO}_{4}^{2-}$

So, at equilibrium:

$[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}]=2s_{1},[\mathrm{CrO}_{4}^{2-}]=s_{1}$

Hence,

$K_{sp}=[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}]^{2}[\mathrm{CrO}_{4}^{2-}]$

$32x=(2s_{1})^{2}(s_{1})=4s_{1}^{3}$

$s_{1}^{3}=8x$

$s_{1}=2\sqrt{3x}$

Now let the molar solubility of $\mathrm{AgBr}$ be $s_{2}$.

For the dissolution:

$\mathrm{AgBr}(\mathrm{s})⇌\mathrm{Ag}^{+}+\mathrm{Br}^{-}$

So,

$[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}]=s_{2},[\mathrm{Br}^{-}]=s_{2}$

Thus,

$K_{sp}=[\mathrm{Ag}^{+}][\mathrm{Br}^{-}]$

$4y=s_{2}^{2}$

$s_{2}=2\sqrt{y}$

Now the required ratio is:

$\frac{\text{molarity of}\mathrm{Ag}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}}{\text{molarity of}\mathrm{AgBr}}=\frac{s_{1}}{s_{2}}=\frac{2\sqrt{3x}}{2\sqrt{y}}=\frac{\sqrt{3x}}{\sqrt{y}}$

So, the correct answer is:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{3x}}{\sqrt{y}}$

Therefore, Option D is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
An electrochemical cell is constructed using half cells in the direction of spontaneous change:
$Fe(OH)_{2}(s) + 2e^{−}$ → $Fe(s) + 2OH^{−}(aq)      E^{θ} = −0.88 V$
and AgBr$(s) + e^{−}$ → $Ag(s) + Br^{−}(aq)      E^{θ} = +0.07 V$
Which of the following options is correct?
options: Fe is reduced in the electrochemical cell
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a spontaneous electrochemical cell, the half-reaction with higher standard reduction potential undergoes reduction, and the other one undergoes oxidation.

Given half-reactions:

$\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{e}^{-}\to \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})E^{θ}=-0.88\text{V}$

$\mathrm{AgBr}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{e}^{-}\to \mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})E^{θ}=+0.07\text{V}$

Since $+0.07\text{V}>-0.88\text{V}$, the $\mathrm{AgBr}/\mathrm{Ag}$ half-cell will undergo reduction and the iron half-cell will undergo oxidation.

So reverse the iron half-reaction:

$\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})\to \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{e}^{-}$

Multiply the silver half-reaction by $2$:

$2\mathrm{AgBr}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{e}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$

Now add them:

$\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{AgBr}(\mathrm{s})\to \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})+2\mathrm{Br}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})$

This matches Option A.

Now calculate $E_{\text{cell}}^{θ}$:

$E_{\text{cell}}^{θ}=E_{\text{cathode}}^{θ}-E_{\text{anode}}^{θ}$

Here,

cathode: $\mathrm{AgBr}/\mathrm{Ag}$, so $E_{\text{cathode}}^{θ}=+0.07\text{V}$

anode: reduction potential of $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}/\mathrm{Fe}$ is $-0.88\text{V}$

Therefore,

$E_{\text{cell}}^{θ}=0.07-(-0.88)=0.95\text{V}$

So Option B is false.

Option C is false because Fe is oxidised, not reduced.

Option D is false because $E_{\text{cell}}^{θ}$ is an intensive property, not an extensive property.

Hence, the correct option is:

$\text{Option A}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: $t_{100$%} is the time required for the 100% completion of the reaction while $t_{1/2}$ is the time required for 50% of the reaction to be completed. Which of the following option correctly represents the relation between $t_{100$%} and $t_{1/2}$ for zero and first order reactions respectively?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a zero order reaction:

The integrated rate law is

$[A]_{t}=[A]_{0}-kt$

For 100% completion, $[A]_{t}=0$.

So,

$0=[A]_{0}-kt_{100%}$

$t_{100%}=\frac{[A]_{0}}{k}$

For half-life, $[A]_{t}=\frac{[A]_{0}}{2}$.

So,

$\frac{[A]_{0}}{2}=[A]_{0}-kt_{1/2}$

$kt_{1/2}=\frac{[A]_{0}}{2}$

$t_{1/2}=\frac{[A]_{0}}{2k}$

Hence,

$t_{100%}=\frac{[A]_{0}}{k}=2\left (\frac{[A]_{0}}{2k}\right )=2t_{1/2}$

So for zero order,

$t_{100%}=2t_{1/2}$

For a first order reaction:

The integrated rate law is

$[A]_{t}=[A]_{0}e^{-kt}$

For 100% completion, we need $[A]_{t}=0$.

That means

$0=[A]_{0}e^{-kt}$

But $e^{-kt}$ can never become exactly zero for any finite value of $t$.

So, the reaction takes infinite time for complete consumption.

Thus,

$t_{100%}=\infty$

Also, for first order reaction,

$t_{1/2}=\frac{0.693}{k}$

Hence $t_{100%}$ is not a finite multiple of $t_{1/2}$, rather it is effectively represented as infinite.

So the correct relation is:

Zero order: $t_{100%}=2t_{1/2}$

First order: $t_{100%}=(t_{1/2})^{\infty }$ in the given options, meaning complete reaction requires infinite time.

Therefore, the correct option is:

$\text{Option B}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The first ionisation enthalpy of the elements Na, Mg, Cl and Ar follows the order Na > Mg > Cl > Ar.
Statement (II) : Among Ca, Al, Fe and B, the third ionisation enthalpy is very high for Ca.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For Statement (I), let us check the trend of first ionisation enthalpy.

Across a period, first ionisation enthalpy generally increases from left to right because effective nuclear charge increases.

For the elements given:

Na

Mg

Cl

Ar

the correct order of first ionisation enthalpy is

$\text{Na}<\text{Mg}<\text{Cl}<\text{Ar}$

But the statement says

$\text{Na}>\text{Mg}>\text{Cl}>\text{Ar}$

This is clearly wrong.

So, Statement (I) is false.

For Statement (II), we compare the third ionisation enthalpy of Ca, Al, Fe and B.

Third ionisation enthalpy means removal of the third electron, that is, from the species $M^{2+}$.

Now consider calcium:

Ca has electronic configuration  

$[\text{Ar}]4s^{2}$

After losing two electrons,  

$\text{Ca}^{2+}=[\text{Ar}]$

which is a noble gas configuration.

Removing the third electron from $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ means breaking a very stable noble gas configuration, so the third ionisation enthalpy is very high.

Hence, Statement (II) is true.

Therefore:

Statement (I) is false

Statement (II) is true

So, the correct answer is:

$\text{Option D}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements:
 Statement (I): Oxidising power of halogens decreases in the order $F_{2}>Cl_{2}>Br_{2}>I_{2}$, which is the basis of "Layer test".
 Statement (II): "Layer test" to identify $Br_{2}$ and $I_{2}$ in aqueous solution involves the oxidation of bromide or iodide into $Br_{2}$ or $I_{2}$ respectively with $Cl_{2}$, which is a type of displacement redox reaction.
 In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is true: the oxidising power of the halogens falls in the order $\mathrm{F}{}_{2}>\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}>\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}>\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ ($E^{\circ }$ = 2.87, 1.36, 1.09 and 0.54 V), so a halogen oxidises the halide ions of the halogens below it; this is the basis of the layer test.

Statement II is true: chlorine water oxidises bromide or iodide ions, a halogen displacement redox reaction.

$\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}+\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$

$\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{I}{}^{-}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}+\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$

The liberated $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$ or $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ dissolves in the added $\mathrm{CCl}{}_{4}$ (or $\mathrm{CHCl}{}_{3}$) layer and colours it orange-brown or violet respectively, which identifies $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ or $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Which of the following sets includes all the species that will change the orange colour of $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ in acidic medium?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In acidic medium, $\mathrm{K}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}$ acts as a strong oxidising agent.

Its orange colour is due to $\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$, which gets reduced to green $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$:

$\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}+14\mathrm{H}^{+}+6\mathrm{e}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

So, the species that will change the orange colour must be reducing agents, because they will reduce dichromate to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$.

Now check each option.

Option A: $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+},\mathrm{Sn}^{2+},\mathrm{I}^{-},\mathrm{S}^{2-}$

$\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\to \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ : reducing agent

$\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}\to \mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$ : reducing agent

$\mathrm{I}^{-}\to \mathrm{I}_{2}$ : reducing agent

$\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ : strong reducing agent

All these can reduce acidified dichromate, so all will change the orange colour.

Option B: $\mathrm{S}^{2-},\mathrm{Fe}^{3+},\mathrm{I}^{-},\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}$

$\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ : reducing agent

$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ : not a reducing agent here

$\mathrm{I}^{-}$ : reducing agent

$\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}$ : reducing agent

Since $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ will not reduce dichromate, this option is incorrect.

Option C: $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+},\mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-},\mathrm{SO}_{2},\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$

$\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ : reducing agent

$\mathrm{NO}_{2}^{-}$ : can act as reducing agent

$\mathrm{SO}_{2}$ : reducing agent

$\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$ : already in higher oxidation state, not a reducing agent

So this option is incorrect.

Option D: $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+},\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-},\mathrm{S}^{2-},\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$

$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ : not reducing

$\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$ : not reducing

$\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ : reducing

$\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$ : not reducing

So this is also incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is:

$\text{Option A}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : 1,2,3-Trihydroxypropane can be separated from water by simple distillation.
Statement (II) : An azeotropic mixture cannot be separated by fractional distillation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Analysis of Statement (I) : 

1,2,3-Trihydroxypropane is commonly known as glycerol. In the soap industry, it is found mixed with water in a solution called 'spent lye'. Glycerol has a very high boiling point (around $563\text{K}$ or $290^{\circ }\text{C}$) and it has a tendency to decompose at or below its normal boiling point. Because of this risk of decomposition under continuous heating at normal atmospheric pressure, simple distillation cannot be used. 

Instead, the standard technique prescribed for its separation is distillation under reduced pressure (also known as vacuum distillation). By reducing the pressure on the surface of the liquid, the mixture can boil at a much lower temperature, which prevents the glycerol from decomposing. Therefore, Statement (I) is false.

Analysis of Statement (II) :

An azeotrope, or an azeotropic mixture, is defined as a binary mixture having the exact same composition in both the liquid phase and the vapour phase. Because the vapour has the same proportions of components as the unboiled liquid, the mixture boils at a constant temperature, acting almost like a single pure liquid. 

Fractional distillation relies on the principle that the vapour phase will be richer in the more volatile component. Since an azeotropic mixture does not show any change in composition upon vaporization, the components cannot be separated into their pure fractions by fractional distillation. Therefore, Statement (II) is completely true.

Conclusion :

Since Statement (I) is false because distillation under reduced pressure must be used, and Statement (II) is fundamentally true according to the properties of azeotropes, the correct logical match is Option D.

Correct Answer :

Option D : Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Benzyl chloride reacts faster in $S_{N}1$ mechanism than ethyl chloride.
Statement (II) : Ethyl carbocation intermediate is less stabilized by hyperconjugation than benzyl carbocation by resonance.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an $S_{N}1$ reaction, the rate depends on the stability of the carbocation formed after the leaving group departs.

For benzyl chloride:

$\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl}\to \text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{5}\text{CH}_{2}^{+}+\text{Cl}^{-}$

The benzyl carbocation formed is highly stable because the positive charge is delocalised over the benzene ring by resonance.

For ethyl chloride:

$\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{Cl}\to \text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}^{+}+\text{Cl}^{-}$

The ethyl carbocation is much less stable. It gets only slight stabilization by hyperconjugation, which is weaker than resonance stabilization.

So:

Statement (I) is true: benzyl chloride reacts faster than ethyl chloride in the $S_{N}1$ mechanism.

Statement (II) is also true: ethyl carbocation is less stabilized by hyperconjugation than benzyl carbocation by resonance.

Also, Statement (II) correctly explains Statement (I).

Therefore, the correct answer is:

$\text{Option A}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: In IUPAC nomenclature, the correct order of decreasing priority of functional group is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In IUPAC nomenclature, the seniority of functional groups (highest first) is:

$-\mathrm{COOH}>-\mathrm{SO}_{3}\mathrm{H}>-\mathrm{COOR}>-\mathrm{COCl}>-\mathrm{CONH}_{2}>-\mathrm{CN}>-\mathrm{CHO}>>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}>-\mathrm{OH}>-\mathrm{NH}_{2}>>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}<>-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{C}-$

Option (C), amide > aldehyde > ketone > amine > alkyne, follows this sequence.

Option (A) puts the ketone above the aldehyde, option (B) puts the amide above the ester and the amine above the alcohol, and option (D) puts the aldehyde above the nitrile.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
For the given molecule, "x", the preferred site for the attack of the electrophile is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In x (benzanilide, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$) the ring carrying p and r is bonded to the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ group, and the ring carrying s and u is bonded to nitrogen.

The $-\mathrm{CO}-$ group withdraws electrons from its ring ($-M$, $-I$) and deactivates it; p (ortho) and r (para) to the carbonyl lie on this deactivated ring, so electrophilic attack there is not favoured.

The $-\mathrm{NH}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ group donates the nitrogen lone pair into the other ring ($+M$), activating it and directing the electrophile to its ortho (s) and para (u) positions; the lone pair is partly delocalised onto $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$, so the activation is moderate, as in acetanilide.

The bulky $-\mathrm{NHCOC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ group hinders the ortho position s sterically, so substitution occurs predominantly at the para position u.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Match List - I with List - II.

  
    
    List - I 
Mixture of Compounds
    
    List - II
Reagent used to distinguish
  
  
    A
    Diethyl amine + Ethyl amine
    I
    Bromine water
  
  
    B
    Acetaldehyde + Acetone
    II
    CHCl₃ + KOH, Δ
  
  
    C
    Ethanol + Phenol
    III
    Neutral FeCl₃
  
  
    D
    Benzoic acid + Cinnamic acid
    IV
    Ammoniacal silver nitrate
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Diethyl amine + Ethyl amine (A):

Ethyl amine ($CH_{3}CH_{2}NH_{2}$) is a primary ($1^{\circ }$) aliphatic amine, whereas diethyl amine ($(CH_{3}CH_{2})_{2}NH$) is a secondary ($2^{\circ }$) aliphatic amine. Primary amines answer the Carbylamine test (or isocyanide test). When warmed with chloroform ($CHCl_{3}$) and alcoholic potassium hydroxide ($KOH$), primary amines produce a foul-smelling substance called isocyanide. Secondary and tertiary amines do not show this reaction.

Therefore, A matches with II.

Acetaldehyde + Acetone (B):

Acetaldehyde ($CH_{3}CHO$) is an aldehyde, while acetone ($CH_{3}COCH_{3}$) is a ketone. Aldehydes can be distinguished from ketones using Tollens' test. When treated with Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate), aldehydes get oxidized to carboxylate ions, and the silver ions are reduced to form a brilliant silver mirror on the inner walls of the test tube. Ketones do not respond to this test. 

Therefore, B matches with IV.

Ethanol + Phenol (C):

Phenol ($C_{6}H_{5}OH$) has an $OH$ group attached directly to an aromatic ring, which gives a characteristic violet or purple colouration when treated with Neutral $FeCl_{3}$ solution due to the formation of a coordination complex. Ethanol ($CH_{3}CH_{2}OH$), being an aliphatic alcohol, does not react with neutral $FeCl_{3}$. 

Therefore, C matches with III.

Benzoic acid + Cinnamic acid (D):

Cinnamic acid ($C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-COOH$) is an unsaturated acid as it contains a carbon-carbon double bond in its side chain. It responds to the test for unsaturation and will rapidly decolorize the reddish-brown colour of Bromine water. Benzoic acid ($C_{6}H_{5}COOH$) does not have any aliphatic unsaturation and thus will not decolorize bromine water.

Therefore, D matches with I.

To summarize the correct matching:

A $\to$ II

B $\to$ IV

C $\to$ III

D $\to$ I

Comparing this with the given choices, it corresponds exactly to Option D.

Correct Answer:

Option D

A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

text:
Consider the three aromatic molecules (P, Q and R) whose structures have been given below :

[IMG]
The correct order regarding the reactivity of these compounds with $\mathrm{Ph}-\mathrm{N}_{(+)}\equiv \mathrm{N}\mathrm{Cl}^{(-)}$ under optimum but slightly acidic medium is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The correct order is $P>Q>R$, so Option A is correct.

Benzenediazonium chloride undergoes azo coupling, an electrophilic substitution reaction. The aromatic ring attacks the diazonium ion, mainly at the para position to the $-\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}$ group.

The nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance. This increases the electron density of the ring and makes it more reactive towards coupling.

The important difference here is steric inhibition of resonance:

In $P$, there are no ortho methyl groups. The nitrogen lone pair can overlap effectively with the ring, giving strong resonance activation.

In $Q$, one ortho methyl group crowds the $-\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}$ group and reduces its effective overlap with the ring.

In $R$, two ortho methyl groups cause greater crowding. The amino group is twisted further out of the ring plane, so its resonance donation is reduced the most.

Although methyl groups are electron-releasing, the loss of resonance activation due to steric crowding is the dominant effect here. Hence, under the stated coupling conditions,

$P>Q>R$

text:
5.33 g of CrCl$_{3}$·$6H_{2}O$, which is a 1 : 3 electrolyte, is dissolved in water and is passed through a cation exchanger. The chloride ions in the eluted solution, on treatment with AgNO$_{3}$ results in 8.61 g of AgCl. The ratio of moles of complex reacted and moles of AgCl formed is $________ × 10^{-2}. ($Nearest integer)

[Molar mass in g mol$^{–1} Cr$ : 52, Ag : 108, Cl : 35.5, H : 1, O : 16]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the compound be of the type

$[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{x}\text{Cl}_{y}]\text{Cl}_{3-y}\cdot n\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$

Since it is a $1:3$ electrolyte, it gives a total of $4$ ions in solution.

So, the complex must be:

$[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{6}]\text{Cl}_{3}$

because this dissociates as

$[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})_{6}]^{3+}+3\text{Cl}^{-}$

Now calculate moles of the complex.

Molar mass of $\text{CrCl}_{3}\cdot 6\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$:

$=52+3(35.5)+6(18)$

$=52+106.5+108=266.5\text{g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of complex taken:

$\frac{5.33}{266.5}=0.02\text{mol}$

Now, mass of AgCl formed $=8.61\text{g}$

Molar mass of AgCl:

$108+35.5=143.5\text{g mol}^{-1}$

Moles of AgCl formed:

$\frac{8.61}{143.5}=0.06\text{mol}$

Required ratio:

$\frac{\text{moles of complex reacted}}{\text{moles of AgCl formed}}=\frac{0.02}{0.06}=\frac{1}{3}=0.3333$

Now express this as

$x\times 10^{-2}$

So,

$0.3333=33.33\times 10^{-2}$

Nearest integer $=33$.

Final answer:

$33$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Consider the isomers of hydrocarbon with molecular formula $C_{5}H_{10}$. These isomers do not decolourise $KMnO_{4}$ solution. These isomers are subjected to chlorination with chlorine in presence of light to give monochloro compounds. The total number of monochloro compounds (structural isomers only) formed is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Isomers of $\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}$ that do not decolourise $\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}$ have no C=C bond, so they are the five cycloalkanes. The number of structural monochloro products of each equals its number of distinct kinds of H atom.

Cyclopentane: all H equivalent, 1 product.

Methylcyclobutane: Cl on the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, on ring C-1, on ring C-2 or on ring C-3, 4 products.

Ethylcyclopropane: Cl on the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, on the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ of the ethyl group, on ring C-1 or on ring C-2, 4 products.

1,1-Dimethylcyclopropane: Cl on a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ or on a ring $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$, 2 products.

1,2-Dimethylcyclopropane: Cl on a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, on a ring CH (C-1) or on the ring $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ (C-3), 3 products.


[IMG]

$1+4+4+2+3=14$

Hence, the answer is 14.

text: One mole of an alkane (x) requires 8 mole oxygen for complete combustion. Sum of number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the alkane (x) is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an alkane, the general formula is

$C_{n}H_{2n+2}$

The combustion reaction of an alkane is

$C_{n}H_{2n+2}+\frac{3n+1}{2}O_{2}\to nCO_{2}+(n+1)H_{2}O$

Given that 1 mole of the alkane requires 8 moles of oxygen, so

$\frac{3n+1}{2}=8$

Now solve:

$3n+1=16$

$3n=15$

$n=5$

So the alkane is

$C_{5}H_{12}$

Now, total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms is

$5+12=17$

So, the required answer is

$17$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
For reaction A → P, rate constant $k=1.5\times 10^{3}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ at $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$
If activation energy for the above reaction is $60\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, then the temperature (in ${}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$) at which rate constant, $k=4.5\times 10^{3}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ is $______. ($Nearest integer)
Given : $\log 2=0.30$, $\log 3=0.48$, $R=8.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, $\ln 10=2.3$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Use the Arrhenius equation in its two-temperature form:

$\ln \left (\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}\right )=\frac{E_{a}}{R}\left (\frac{1}{T_{1}}-\frac{1}{T_{2}}\right )$

Given:

$k_{1}=1.5\times 10^{3}\mathrm{s}^{-1},T_{1}=27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}=300\mathrm{K}$

$k_{2}=4.5\times 10^{3}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$

$E_{a}=60\mathrm{kJ}\quad \mathrm{mol}^{-1}=60000\mathrm{J}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$R=8.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

First, find the ratio:

$\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}=\frac{4.5\times 10^{3}}{1.5\times 10^{3}}=3$

So,

$\ln 3=\frac{60000}{8.3}\left (\frac{1}{300}-\frac{1}{T_{2}}\right )$

Now convert $\ln 3$ using the given values:

$\ln 3=2.3\log 3=2.3\times 0.48=1.104$

Also,

$\frac{60000}{8.3}\approx 7229$

Hence,

$1.104=7229\left (\frac{1}{300}-\frac{1}{T_{2}}\right )$

Therefore,

$\frac{1}{300}-\frac{1}{T_{2}}=\frac{1.104}{7229}$

$\frac{1.104}{7229}\approx 1.53\times 10^{-4}$

So,

$\frac{1}{T_{2}}=\frac{1}{300}-1.53\times 10^{-4}$

$\frac{1}{300}=3.33\times 10^{-3}$

Thus,

$\frac{1}{T_{2}}=3.33\times 10^{-3}-0.153\times 10^{-3}=3.18\times 10^{-3}$

$T_{2}\approx \frac{1}{3.18\times 10^{-3}}\approx 314\mathrm{K}$

Now convert into Celsius:

$t=314-273=41^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$

Hence, the required temperature is

$41^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: At the transition temperature $T$, $A⇌B$ and $\Delta G^{0}=105-35\log T$ where A and B are two states of substance X. The transition temperature in ${}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ when pressure is 1 atm is $________. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At the transition temperature, the two states $A$ and $B$ are in equilibrium.

So, for the equilibrium condition,

$\Delta G^{0}=0$

Given:

$\Delta G^{0}=105-35\log T$

At transition temperature,

$105-35\log T=0$

Now solve:

$35\log T=105$

$\log T=\frac{105}{35}=3$

So,

$T=10^{3}=1000\text{K}$

Now convert into degree Celsius:

$T(^{\circ }\mathrm{C})=1000-273=727^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$

Nearest integer:

$727$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift
